title: T38.2 DeepSearch SSE Triage & Project Stats Bug Report

deepsearch_sse.summary: DeepSearch SSE infrastructure is fully implemented and functional. The 'disconnected' status is an infrastructure availability issue — the DeepSearch worker is not deployed/running, not a code defect.
deepsearch_sse.root_cause: DeepSearch worker (external service) is offline. TraceLab SSE endpoints are correctly registered, authenticated, and tested.

timeline.T33.4: SSE infrastructure established: event bus, /events/stream endpoint, frontend MissionActivityFeed component, 12 tests
timeline.T34.3: SSE auth fixed: added require_authenticated_user_sse() supporting JWT via query param for EventSource compatibility
timeline.current: Endpoints return 401 without auth (correct behavior). Events flow when worker is active.

endpoints_registered: GET /api/v1/missions/events/stream — SSE stream with JWT query param auth

deepsearch_sse.decision: No code fix needed. DeepSearch SSE shows 'disconnected' because the external DeepSearch worker service is not running. When deployed, events will flow through the established pipeline. No deprecation warranted — the architecture is sound.
deepsearch_sse.recommendation: Deploy DeepSearch worker or configure DEEPSEARCH_API_URL to resolve the 'disconnected' status. The code path is fully operational.

project_stats_bug.summary: Cache key collision bug was identified and fixed in T34.2 (commit aa32f9d).
project_stats_bug.root_cause: project_metadata_key() in cache_manager.py did not differentiate stats requests by project_id, causing all projects to share the same cache slot.

fix_applied.change: Added 'if kind == "stats" and identifier: return ("stats", identifier)' to produce unique per-project cache keys

project_stats_bug.decision: No further action needed. Bug was fixed in Sprint 34 with proper test coverage.
